title: SAURABH DORA versus STATE OF UTTARAKHAND
judges: ["Hon'ble Mr. Justice Ravindra Maithani,Hon'ble Mr. Justice Siddhartha Sah"]

paras.text:
UKHC010148032026
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Habeas Corpus No. 38 of 2026
Saurabh Dora --Petitioner
Versus
State Of Uttarakhand and Another
--Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Gaurav Kandpal, learned counsel for the petitioner through
video conferencing.
Mr. B.N. Molakhi, learned DAG for the State.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Coram: Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Hon'ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
Instant petition has been filed by the petitioner
seeking the custody of his minor child, Km. Nanika Dora.
2. According to the petitioner, he and respondent
No.2 were married on 16.04.2017. They were blessed
with two girls. The younger daughter passed away on
12.11.2022. The elder one, Km. Nanika Dora, is the
corpus, who was born on 15.12.2018. Parties have
strained relationships. They started staying separately,
but the petitioner's interaction with the minor child was
completely restricted. The petitioner made repeated
requests to meet the corpus and maintain ordinary
parental interaction through telephonic and video calls,
but such requests were consistently declined.
3. It is further the case of the petitioner that
respondent no.2 has already instituted a custody of
children case under Section 35 of the Uniform Civil Code,
Uttarakhand, 2024, bearing the Case No.126 of 2025,
1

UKHC010148032026
before the learned Principal Judge, Family Court,
Dehradun ("the Case"). The petitioner has already
appeared in the case and moved an application seeking
visitation and telephonic/video call access with the minor
child, but that application is still pending. With these
and other averments, the petitioner seeks directions that
State of Uttarakhand may be directed to secure the
custody of the corpus from the custody of respondent
no.2 and produce her before this Court.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner
and perused the records.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner would
submit that though the child custody case has already
been filed by respondent no.2 in the competent court, but
an application seeking visitation rights filed by the
petitioner has yet not been decided by the concerned
court despite lapse of considerable time. The remedy has
become ineffective. He would further submit that Habeas
Corpus Petitions are very much maintainable even during
the pendency of the child custody cases, where the
remedy in the child custody cases is ineffective. He
referred to the principle of law as laid down by the
Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Tejaswini Gaud
and Others vs. Shekhar Jagdish Prasad Tewari and
Others, (2019) 7 SCC 42, particularly reference has
been made to paragraph 19 of the judgment, which reads
as follows :-
"19. Habeas corpus proceedings is not to justify
or examine the legality of the custody. Habeas
corpus proceedings is a medium through which
the custody of the child is addressed to the
discretion of the Court. Habeas corpus is a
prerogative writ which is an extraordinary
remedy and the writ is issued where in the
circumstances of the particular case, ordinary
remedy provided by the law is either not
2

UKHC010148032026
available or is ineffective; otherwise a writ will
not be issued. In child custody matters, the
power of the High Court in granting the writ is
qualified only in cases where the detention of a
minor by a person who is not entitled to his
legal custody. In view of the pronouncement on
the issue in question by the Supreme Court and
the High Courts, in our view, in child custody
matters, the writ of habeas corpus is
maintainable where it is proved that the
detention of a minor child by a parent or others
was illegal and without any authority of law."
6. Reading from the above paragraph, it is argued
that since the application seeking visitation rights filed
by the petitioner in the case is still pending that remedy
has become ineffective, hence indulgence of this Court is
required.
7. In child custody matters, the paramount
consideration is the interest of the child, which depends
on various factors; economic and social status of the
parties, their relationship with the child, the overall
development of the child etc. Undoubtedly, a writ petition
is maintainable in certain circumstances, but not as a
general rule. In the case of Tejaswini Gaud (Supra)
itself, in para 19, which is quoted hereinabove in the last
line, the Court has held; 'The writ of habeas corpus is
maintainable where it is proved that the detention of
a minor child by a parent or others was illegal and
without any authority of law". In the instant case, the
custody of the child is with the mother; how can it be
termed as illegal or without any authority of law?
8. In fact, in para 14 of the judgment in the case
of Tejaswini Gaud (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court
observed as follows :-
"14. Writ of habeas corpus is a prerogative
process for securing the liberty of the subject by
affording an effective means of immediate
3

UKHC010148032026
release from an illegal or improper detention.
The writ also extends its influence to restore the
custody of a minor to his guardian when
wrongfully deprived of it. The detention of a
minor by a person who is not entitled to his
legal custody is treated as equivalent to illegal
detention for the purpose of granting writ,
directing custody of the minor child. For
restoration of the custody of a minor from a
person who according to the personal law, is not
his legal or natural guardian, in appropriate
cases, the writ court has jurisdiction."
9. The above observation by Hon'ble the Supreme
Court makes it further clear that in habeas corpus
petitions, indulgence could be made if the custody is not
legal or not with the natural guardian. Not only this, in
the case of Nirmala v. Kulwant Singh and Others,
(2024) 10 SCC 595, the Hon'ble Apex Court has followed
the principles of law laid down in Tejaswini Gaud
(Supra) and in para 27 observed as follows:
"27. It can thus be seen that no hard-and-fast rule
can be laid down insofar as the maintainability of
a habeas corpus petition in the matters of custody
of a minor child is concerned. As to whether the
writ court should exercise its extraordinary
jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of
India or not will depend on the facts and
circumstances of each case."

10. Respondent no.2, the wife of the petitioner, has
already filed a custody case in the court of competent
jurisdiction, where the petitioner has already filed an
application seeking visitation rights. The custody with
the mother cannot be termed illegal or without authority
of law. Over and above, she is also the natural guardian.
11. In such view of the matter, definitely, the
jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India
may not be invoked. Accordingly, this Court sees no
reason to make any interference in the writ petition and
4

UKHC010148032026
it deserves to be dismissed at the stage of admission
itself.
12. The Habeas Corpus Petition is hereby
dismissed in limine.
